video.description: New cat alert! A call from a wildlife sanctuary about a "weird cat" has led to the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years. Smaller than an average housecat and covered in leopard-like spots, the cat species—proposed name Leopardus tilcayo—lives in Bolivia’s Yungas forest ecoregion, and very little is known about its day-to-day life in the wild. Its discovery is redrawing the branches of the cat family tree, and researchers hope the methods used to identify it could be used to find even more new cat species around the world. Learn more about this feline surprise at the 🔗 in bio.

analysis.summary: National Geographic announces the discovery of *Leopardus tilcayo*, the first new wild cat species identified in over a century, found in Bolivia's Yungas forest.

story.premise: A wildlife sanctuary's report of an unusual spotted cat leads to a major zoological discovery.
arc: Scientists identify a mysterious spotted feline reported by a sanctuary.
The animal is confirmed as a previously unknown species distinct from known cats.
The new species, named *Leopardus tilcayo*, is smaller than a housecat with leopard-like spots.
It inhabits the remote Yungas forest ecoregion in Bolivia.
Little is currently known about its daily behavior or life in the wild.
The discovery reshapes the evolutionary family tree of the cat species.
Researchers hope their identification methods will help find more hidden species globally.
